fields.meta_description: See accounts receivable automation in four examples: overdue reminders, payment matching, short payments, and credit holds. Build yours free.
fields.h1: Build Accounts Receivable Automation for Every Open Invoice
fields.hero_description: Build accounts receivable automation that chases overdue invoices, matches payments, and holds orders from late accounts.
fields.features_heading: The Follow-Up Work Behind Every Invoice
fields.features_subheading: An invoice is half the job until the cash arrives. Emergent builds the app that chases and matches, and your team makes the calls.
fields.feature_1:
Reminders timed to the due date

You set when each email goes out, before and after the due date, and who receives it. A tighter schedule for one large customer takes a single sentence in a new prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Remittances read into matches

The app reads the remittance attached to a payment and lines up each invoice number with an open invoice. A line it cannot read clearly waits for a person to confirm it.
fields.feature_3:
Every exception has a named owner

Short payments and unmatched deposits go to the person you name for each, never a shared inbox. That person gets a Slack message or an email, and a reminder if it sits untouched.
fields.feature_4:
Credit limits checked at the order

Before a new order ships, the app checks the age of the customer's oldest open invoice. An order that breaks your rule waits for an approver, who releases it or keeps the hold.
fields.feature_5:
Aging and DSO on one dashboard

Open balances update by customer and age bucket as payments post. Days sales outstanding sits beside them, and the effect of each new rule shows up in the number you report.
fields.feature_6:
Synced with your accounting system

Invoices and payment records sync with QuickBooks, Xero, or NetSuite through their APIs. Your ledger stays the record, and each payment the app applies is written back.

fields.usecase_heading: Four AR Jobs a Finance Team Hands Off First
fields.tab_content_1:
Seven days late, the second email and a call task

Larkspur Supply bills Calloway Bistro $4,860.00 on invoice INV-3318. Three days before the due date, the app emails the invoice to Nadia Okonjo in Calloway's AP team. The due date passes unpaid. At 7 days past due, a second email goes to Nadia, and account owner Wes Abernathy gets a task to call her.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three invoices closed by one deposit

A $12,940.00 ACH deposit lands from Halvorsen Inns with a remittance PDF attached. The app reads the PDF, finds INV-3290, INV-3301, and INV-3307 on it, and matches each line to its open invoice. All three are marked paid, and the payment posts to QuickBooks with the remittance saved beside it.
fields.tab_content_3:
A $300 shortfall lands with the sales rep

Pinecrest Catering pays $2,700.00 against INV-3312, a $3,000.00 invoice, with a note: 2 cases returned damaged. The app applies the payment and leaves $300.00 open, tagged Disputed. Imogen Hale, the sales rep on the account, gets the balance with the note attached and decides on a credit or a follow-up.
fields.tab_content_4:
When an invoice passes 60 days, new orders wait

Brightwater Grill places order SO-7741 for $2,350.00 while its invoice INV-3204 for $1,980.00 is 64 days past due. Your rule puts any account with an invoice over 60 days late on credit hold. The order stops before it ships. Controller Tobias Mwangi sees both amounts in the app and decides whether it goes out.

fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan accounts receivable automation around your aging report, then build and test it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Connect the ledger and the bank
fields.howto_step_1_des: Run your aging report and sort customers by how late their oldest invoice is. Note which accounts sit past 30 days and why: a missed reminder or a dispute nobody owns. That list sets the first jobs to automate.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe the schedule the way you would explain it to a new hire: one email 3 days before the due date, a second at 7 days late, a call after that. Emergent builds the app and its logic from those sentences.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect your accounting system and the inbox or bank feed where payments and remittances arrive, through their APIs. Keep the ledger as the record of each invoice, and have the app write every applied payment back to it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide what counts as a match: the invoice number on the remittance, the exact amount, or both. A payment that fits no open invoice should land in a queue with the deposit and the remittance side by side.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name one person for each kind of exception. Short payments go to the sales rep who knows the customer, held orders go to the controller, and unmatched deposits go to whoever applies cash today.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick last month's payments and run them through before the app touches a live account. Check each match against what your team posted by hand, fix a rule by prompting, and run the month again until the two agree.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Switch on the reminder schedule before the matching rules, since an email changes no balance. Watch the aging report for 30 days, compare the past-due total with the month before, then turn on the next automation.

faq_plan.a: Accounts receivable automation is the use of software to run the tasks involved in collecting money customers owe a business. Payment reminders go out on a schedule, and incoming payments are matched against the invoices they settle. A person still handles the accounts that need a conversation.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up accounts receivable automation?
faq_plan.a: Pick the one job that costs your team the most hours, then describe it in Emergent's AI automation builder, one rule per sentence. Say when reminders go out, what counts as a payment match, and who decides on a short payment. Emergent builds the app with its database and dashboard and connects it to your accounting system through its API.

faq_plan.q: What is the best software for automating accounts receivable?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best software for automating accounts receivable?

prov.original: What is the best software for automating accounts receivable?

faq_plan.a: No single product is best for every team; the right one fits the step where your invoices stall. HighRadius uses AI-driven workflows to automate collections, cash application, deductions, and payment forecasting. BILL lets a business set up automated reminders on the invoices it sends. Compare each against your own aging report before you commit.

faq_plan.q: Does accounts receivable automation software also handle accounts payable?
faq_plan.a: Some products do and some do not: certain platforms run receivables and payables in one place, while others cover only the money customers owe you. On the receivables side, the software chases and applies customer payments; accounts payable automation handles the bills you owe vendors. Check which side a product covers before you compare prices.

faq_plan.q: What does AR automation do with a payment that matches no invoice?
faq_plan.a: AR automation puts it in a queue for a person instead of guessing where it belongs. The queue shows the deposit next to any remittance that came with it, and whoever applies cash picks the invoice or contacts the customer. In an app Emergent builds, each choice made in that queue is saved to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Does AR automation software replace your accounting system?
faq_plan.a: Plan for it to sit beside your ledger rather than replace it, and keep the accounting system as the book of record. Have the AR automation software pull open invoices from that ledger and post each payment back once it is matched. An app Emergent builds runs that two-way sync through the ledger's API.

faq_plan.q: What are the main accounts receivable automation benefits?
faq_plan.a: The main benefits are reminders that never get skipped and payments applied the day they arrive. Both show up in days sales outstanding, which measures receivables in average sales days rather than dollars. Pair it with invoice automation, and the clock on each invoice starts the day the work is billed.

faq_plan.q: How do you choose an accounts receivable automation solution?
faq_plan.a: Choose by the step where your cash waits longest, then test how the solution handles exceptions there. Ask what happens to a short payment or an unmatched deposit, and who sees it first. Price it at month-end volume. An app built with Emergent runs with no task cap.

faq_plan.q: What is accounts receivable invoice automation?
faq_plan.a: Accounts receivable invoice automation is the part of AR automation that creates and sends each invoice, then tracks it until it is paid. The invoice is built from the order or timesheet, emailed to the customer's AP contact, and logged with its send date. Reminders then count days from that date.

faq_plan.q: Which steps of the accounts receivable process should automation cover first?
faq_plan.a: Start with payment matching if your team spends hours applying cash, and with reminders if invoices sit unpaid. Credit holds come later, once your rules for late accounts are agreed. The same build order holds for other finance workflows, such as an automated loan processing system: test on past files first, then go live one rule at a time.
